## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column holds the start time of processes that are still running, so it must be fixed before merge. Its documented NULL meaning also fails for processes that were started and then cleared.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file at the repository root.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — finished_at is filled from the 'started' event, not a finish — For process 20, whose latest event is `started`, `finished_at` is `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, although the process has not finished. `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `created`, `started` and `cleared`, so no event marks a finish; `models/schema.yml:11` still says "Timestamp when the process finished." — Consumers will treat running processes as finished at their start time and will compute wrong durations and completion states. — Fix: If the column should be the start time, rename it to `started_at` and update `models/schema.yml:11`; if it should be a finish time, decide which event type marks a finish before you add the column.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — NULL does not mean never started — Process 30 (`started`, then `cleared`) gets NULL because `models/processes.sql:10` reads only the latest event, but the docstring says "NULL means the process has never been started." Line 14 of the same docstring ("Only the most recent event contributes to this row") contradicts line 17. — Consumers will report processes that were started and then cleared as never started. — Fix: Either compute the value across the partition, e.g. `max(case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end) over (partition by process_id)` in `latest_event`, or change line 17 to say NULL means the latest event is not `started`.
